trial_title: Fenofibrate in Type 2 Diabetes- Novel Biomarkers and Mechanisms

inclusion_criteria.text: Male or female aged ≥18 and ≤ 70 years
Type 2 diabetes of at least one year's duration; stable glycemic control (no more than 1.0% change in HbA1c in the previous six months, but no limit on HbA1c)
Triglycerides >150 mg/dL (in the previous six months)

exclusion_criteria.text: Previous use of Fenofibrate or other fibrates
Recent cardiac event or congestive heart failure

visits.text: Regularly scheduled Endocrinology clinic visit: informed consent and HIPAA form
Visit 1 at the SCTR NEXUS clinic

procedures.text: Women of childbearing potential will have urine β-HCG measured
Fasting blood (80ml) for labs: BUN, Cr, urine microalbumin, LFTs, CPK, Lipid Profile, HbA1c, TSH, C-peptide
Study medication: 160 mg fenofibrate taken orally daily for six weeks
Assessment of adverse events and study drug compliance by pill count
Plasma proteomic signature by LC-MS/MS before and after fenofibrate treatment

safety_information.text: Women of childbearing potential will be required to use acceptable methods for birth control throughout the study
Participants will receive instruction on possible side effects and proper protocol for reporting unexpected symptoms
Risks associated with drawing blood from the arm include momentary discomfort and/or bruising. Infection, excess bleeding, clotting, or fainting is possible, although unlikely.
Serious adverse events will be reported within 24 per MUSC IRB guidelines
If at any time the participant experiences unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, study medication should be discontinued.
Hazards of venipuncture: pain, bruising, inflammation or clot formation, syncope.
Fenofibrate use has been associated with an increased risk of muscle pain, abnormal results in tests of liver function and allergic reaction.
